scope: Initial evidence-backed census of contract-like interfaces and JSON schemas declared inside the pinned atc-engineering source tree. This is not an exhaustive interface inventory and does not establish organization-wide producer/consumer coverage.

contracts.name: Evidence record serialization
contracts.rationale: The implementation declares the schema ID/version and serialization/validation methods, and a matching versioned JSON Schema exists. No automated serialization-to-schema conformance test or complete consumer mapping is established by this inventory.

contracts.name: Finding registry
contracts.rationale: The pinned implementation defines the finding lifecycle, rejects duplicate IDs, and emits a registry document with schema ATC-FND-001/version 1.0.0 through FindingRegistry::write_json. The emitted top-level field set is compatible by inspection with the versioned schema, but no executable instance-to-schema conformance test has been established. No concrete consumer of the persisted registry file is bound in this census.

contracts.name: AI code-agent verification evidence
contracts.rationale: The schema requires commit-bound check evidence and forbids merge authorization, but a direct producer/consumer binding and a source-to-schema validation run have not been established here.

contracts.name: Cross-repository integration graph edge contract
contracts.rationale: The Rust graph implementation and integration document declare named cross-repository contracts, but the edge-level producer/consumer mappings are not reconciled against versioned interfaces or schemas. A non-empty contract name is not proof of a versioned interface.

limitations: The inventory covers only four initially identified declarations in the pinned atc-engineering tree; it is not a complete census of every API, ABI, event, file format, CLI, or cross-repository boundary.
Blob SHAs bind the listed source/schema files to the stated source commit; they do not prove semantic completeness or runtime compatibility.
Unmapped producer/consumer counts describe this inventory only and must not be interpreted as organization-wide totals.
No contract is marked VERIFIED or RECONCILED; consumer mapping, schema conformance, normative registry binding, and organization-wide ownership remain open.
